title: Azoth calculation spec
description: A calculation spec: what a calc is called, the equation, its inputs and outputs, both implementations, a worked example and the tests that exercise it.

id.description: Dotted identifier, e.g. hydraulics.darcy_weisbach. Must match the module and function names in both implementations.

name.description: Human-readable name, used as the doc page title.

equation.description: The equation, in Python expression syntax so the worked example can be re-derived from it. For an implicit equation it is the defining relation, solved with the scheme named in `solver`.

latex.description: The equation in LaTeX, typeset for the generated documentation. A separate field from `equation`, which is Python source used to re-derive the worked example; both are required.

source.description: Where the equation comes from. Only `standard` is required; omit `equation`, `doi` or `url` when they are unknown rather than writing a placeholder.

standard.description: Name of the standard, textbook, or paper.

equation.description: Equation number within the source. Omit the key when the number is not known.

inputs.description: Input quantities, keyed by parameter name. Key names must match the function signatures in both implementations exactly.

outputs.description: Output quantities, keyed by result field name. Key names must match the result struct fields in both implementations exactly.

valid_range.description: Bounds on the range in which the calc is validated. Stated as typed bounds rather than free-form expressions, so they are machine-checkable.

assumptions.description: Physical assumptions the calc relies on that are NOT checked at runtime. Documented, not enforced - keep checked constraints in valid_range.

references.description: Citations. Cite equations and papers; never reproduce copyrighted tables or text.

solver.description: The solver for an implicit equation: the scheme, its tolerance, iteration cap and stopping rule. Both implementations must run exactly this scheme.

kind.description: The scheme to solve with. `fixed_point` iterates from a declared start; `cubic_roots` forms the roots analytically. A kind is admitted only when both implementations run it.

initial_guess.description: Where the iteration starts. Required when `kind` is `fixed_point`; not used by `cubic_roots`, so it is required conditionally rather than always.

convergence.description: Stopping rule applied to successive iterates x_k. `relative` means |x_{k+1} - x_k| <= tolerance * |x_{k+1}|; `absolute` means |x_{k+1} - x_k| <= tolerance.

allOf.comment: fixed_point iterates from a declared start, so it has to declare one

data.description: Repo-relative paths to data files this calc reads. One key per dataset.

worked_example.description: A fully specified example whose expected outputs are independently reproducible from the equation. This is the primary validation artefact.

source.description: Where the example comes from. Use 'derived from the equation above' when we computed it ourselves, and say so in `derivation`.

derivation.description: How the expected values were obtained. Required when source is our own derivation, so a reviewer can retrace it.

inputs.description: Input values in the units declared in `inputs`. Keys must be exactly the calc's input names, so the generated test can call the implementation directly.

expected.description: Expected output values in the units declared in `outputs`.

tests.description: Tests to generate and run. Every calc needs at least a worked_example; reference and property tests are strongly encouraged.

citation.description: Where a value came from, for a reader. Optional everywhere and validated nowhere: the engineer supplying data is responsible for knowing its provenance and whether they may use it.

value.description: A scalar quantity, a symbolic value for an enum or string input, or a list of identifiers for list-valued inputs such as a fitting list.

unit.description: Canonical unit of a quantity in the equation, SI-first; it is the unit the spec and generated docs speak in, and API callers may pass any convertible unit. The enum is generated from `specs/vocabulary/vocabulary.toml` by `tools/gen_vocabulary.py`.

type.description: quantity = a physical quantity carrying a unit. enum = a symbolic result such as a flow regime. fitting_list = one or more fitting ids resolved against the spec's `data.fittings` file.

values.description: Allowed values when type is enum.

fields.description: The named sub-quantities of one record, for `record_list`. Required when type is `record_list`; a result returning structured rows - one per fitting, per component, per phase - needs its row shape declared.

optional.description: Optional inputs may be omitted; the implementation must then emit a RANGE_CHECK_SKIPPED warning for any range check that depends on them, rather than silently passing.

interval.description: The input is a temperature *difference* rather than an absolute temperature. Marking it makes the Python boundary refuse an offset unit (degC, degF); only meaningful on a unit that can express a difference, which is K, and spec_lint enforces that.

allOf.comment: boolean and string carry no unit
record_list requires the shape of one row

quantity.description: Name of the quantity being bounded. Must be an input, an output, a derived quantity, or a state keyword such as `phase`.

computed_from.description: For derived quantities (e.g. Re), the inputs it is computed from. spec_lint uses this to prove the check is actually evaluable.

min.description: Lower bound of the interval described by min/max.

max.description: Upper bound of the interval described by min/max.

when.description: Which side of the min/max interval counts as a violation. 'outside' (the default) means the interval is the ALLOWED range; 'inside' inverts this, for conditions that are only a problem within a band. Only meaningful with min/max.

severity.description: error = mathematically undefined or invalid input, the implementation raises. warning = defined but outside the validated range, the implementation returns a value carrying a warning.

code.description: Which warning code a violation emits. Defaults to OUT_OF_VALID_RANGE; override it when the violation has a more specific meaning, e.g. the transitional-flow band emits TRANSITIONAL_FLOW.

type.description: worked_example = the example above, re-generated into both languages. reference = an independent published or cross-method value. property = an invariant such as unit round-trip or symmetry.

status.description: skipped requires skip_reason. A skipped test is still generated, marked and reported - it is never silently dropped.

skip_reason.description: Why this test does not run, e.g. 'source_needed: citation could not be verified'.

property.description: Which invariant to check, when type is property.

source.description: Citation for the expected values, when type is reference.

allOf.comment: reference tests carry their own inputs and expected values, but only when they actually run - a skipped reference test has no expected values to state
property tests name the invariant they check
